id: The Racket Lounge-The Rogue & Vagabond-Rogue & Vagabond
name: The Racket Lounge
long_description:
Grab a spot on our couch and enjoy the noise at The Racket Lounge - a chill classical music series showcasing up-and-coming Pōneke musicians.

If you’ve never been to a classical concert before, or if you have and now you want to see talented emerging musicians experimenting and playing what they want to play, then The Racket Lounge is for you. Over the past two seasons we’ve seen classical covers, jazz ensembles, video game soundtracks, original compositions, loop pedals, poetry and much more. Our 2026 season is shaping up to be just as epic, plus with your tickets starting at just $5 you can afford to take a chance on something new.

Each concert will feature a different line up of musicians and genres, to be announced a week before each session. If you’re a musician looking to perform at The Racket Lounge, then head to the New Zealand String Quartet’s website to see how to apply.



The Racket Lounge is created and presented by the New Zealand String Quartet Trust - Te Rōpū Tūrū o Aotearoa, New Zealand’s longest-running professional string quartet. With support from Wellington City Council.

Tickets are choose your price starting from just $5.

Please note that Bedlam & Squalor is a licensed venue, so under 18s must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian. Everyone must bring ID.

name: Cumbia Blazera
long_description:
Cumbia Blazera is back at the Rogue on Friday 21 August, eleven players deep and ready to fill the dancefloor. We originated from the Sunday Blazers Football Club and the Sunday Social League, which explains the name and what you're in for: bilingual cumbia built for moving.

We've been quietly working on a follow-up to 2018's album Don't Argue With The Ref, and this gig is your chance to hear a few of the new ones out in the wild, sitting alongside the Latin classics and originals you already know — jangly guitars, punchy brass, and the guero calling the shots as always.

Free entry, music from 9:30pm, FREE ENTRY dogs and rogues and vagabonds all welcome. Come for the cumbia, stay for the company. Vamos a bailar!

id: The Klezmer Rebs-The Rogue & Vagabond-Rogue & Vagabond
name: The Klezmer Rebs
long_description:
The Klezmer Rebs play at Rogue and Vagabond for the first time on Friday night 14 August after a stellar year.

The Rebs bring their sometimes rollicking, sometimes delicate songs from the ‘old country’, hot off headlining at the Wellington Folk Festival and rousing sets at CubaDupa, Newtown Festival, the Undercurrent and Futuna.

They will be featuring tracks from their new live album Back to Futuna. Done miss the unique ethnic world music of the Klezmer Rebs and get your tuchas shaking.

Music from. 9:30, FREE ENTRY - Koha for the band appreciated!

long_description:
After the last concert of his Tour of Australia in Melbourne. Sam Manzanza's Afrobeat Band will be performing his infectious high-energy rhythm at The Rogue and Vagabond on Saturday, 7th March.

Mark in your calendars for an electrifying night of entertainment with Sam Manzanza, the maestro of Afrobeat Afrorock and Afropop.

Get ready to transcend boundaries and immerse yourself in a magical night of love and positive vibes to dance your night away. Nonstop. Satisfaction is guaranteed.

name: Loose Parts
long_description:
Loose Parts is an all new dance-music project led by Jamin Forlong, Alex Vujanic and Sam Hunter, who will be performing live broken beats, jungle and liquid funk music non-stop all throughout the night! Taking inspiration from classic dance floor rhythms and sounds, they will be putting their own spin on club and DJ music via the form of a live band, steeped in jazz and improvisation.

Loose Parts consists of:

Alex Vujanic - saxophone and samples
Jamin Forlong - guitar
Sam Hunter - keyboard
Tyaan Singh - bass
Ateo Buhne - drums

Music from 9:30pm, FREE ENTRY - Koha for the band appreciated!

id: Alex Trask Quintet-The Rogue & Vagabond-Rogue & Vagabond
name: Alex Trask Quintet
long_description:
Local saxophonist Alex Trask presents original music from his various projects, including a recent recording, his first album, and the Lighthouse Trio setlist. Inspired by folk music from around the world and infused with jazz performance practice, these tunes have a simplicity in common. Free improvised sections contrast carefully arranged melodies, allowing creativity and structure to coexist. The fiddle-esque melodies and straightforward harmonies create an open and inviting sound that changes depending on the musicians on stage. Hiding amongst these tunes will be some swing compositions and arrangements of favourite melodies.

Free entry!

Personnel:
Alex Trask - saxophone
Michael Costeloe - trumpet
Duncan Haynes - piano
Seth Boy - bass
Abey Baillie - drums

Photo by Oscar Laven

This week featuring local trumpeters Ben Hunt and Mike Taylor!

Michael Taylor and Ben Hunt pay homage to trumpet masters Freddie Hubbard and Woody Shaw. In this mutually respectful double-trumpet affair, Mike and Ben take on such tunes as Hub-Tones, The Moontrane, and Thermo.
